contracts: list_events returns events overlapping [start,end] with recurrences expanded, sorted by start, local ISO start/end, and calendarId; calendar param matches title or identifier.
Without EventKit full access (authorizationStatus != 3, including write-only 4) list_events raises RuntimeError naming the System Settings > Calendars fix; there is no slow AppleScript fallback.
delete_event deletes the single event in the named calendar whose title contains the given text, starting within ±30 days of now; zero or multiple matches raise ValueError without deleting anything.
add_event/delete_event raise ValueError for an unknown calendar and RuntimeError when EventKit save/remove fails or full access is missing; writes use EKSpanThisEvent with commit=True.
list_events raises ValueError('Calendar not found: <name>') when a named calendar does not exist, instead of returning [] (a silent [] hid a blind-calendar failure).

The child relays failures as {ok:false,error_type,error}; the parent re-raises ValueError/FileNotFoundError by type and everything else as RuntimeError. A worker timeout (60s) or a missing result line raises RuntimeError.

A failing worker exits 1 with a traceback on stderr and the {ok:false,...} line on stdout; the parent returns a result only when the reply is ok AND the exit code is 0. Errors are never swallowed: a missing EventKit import propagates as ImportError (not treated as 'no access'), and unparseable noise_assets JSON raises.

handle_list_events caches results in-process (_list_cache) keyed (start, end, calendar) with a 60s TTL (_CACHE_TTL_S). Only non-empty successes are stored; [] and errors are never cached ([] is what a blind calendar returned). Hits and stores are copies, since _market_watch_events mutates and sorts its list.
handle_add_event and handle_delete_event clear the whole cache before and after the write (also when it fails, since a failed write may still have changed the store).
calendar-list-events-eventkit.description: calendar__list_events, add_event and delete_event go through EventKit (PyObjC); each call runs in a short-lived child process (python -m src.tools.calendar <op>, JSON over stdin/stdout) so no EventKit state survives between calls in the long-lived MCP server. get_events_by_date / get_upcoming_events read market-watch via handle_list_events, so they use the same path and the same cache.
invariants: The TCC Calendars full-access grant belongs to the process running the MCP server, not to the code.

Root cause of the server losing sight of market-watch is unproven; per-call subprocess isolation is a workaround for suspected per-process EventKit state. If blindness recurs with isolation in place, the fallback is a Swift binary per call.

Cache staleness is bounded only by the 60s TTL for changes made outside this server (Calendar.app, iCloud, other devices); only writes through this server invalidate it. The cache is per-process, so a /mcp reconnect empties it.
calendar-list-events-eventkit.name: calendar-list-events-eventkit

contracts: _FOUND_CHECKS maps (domain, action) to a function computing a bool 'found' quality flag from (kwargs, result); calls with no entry record found=None.
Every sync domain__action call — MCP (_wrap) or `mac` CLI (cli-graph _backend.call) — runs through dispatcher.invoke, which wraps the handler in tool_hooks.tool_called(domain, action, kwargs).
Prechecks (_imessage_guard, _mail_guard) run before the handler; a failed precheck raises tool_hooks.Refused (a PermissionError subclass), logs blocked=1 with a reason, and the handler never runs.

A Refused raised by a handler itself (vault path containment in tools/vault.py:_inside_vault) is also logged blocked=1. A plain PermissionError (e.g. from the OS) is logged as an ordinary error, blocked=0.

On success the caller sets holder['result']; _FOUND_CHECKS turns it into a nullable `found` flag stored in mcp_tool_calls.found (contacts__search: found = bool(result), handlers return [] for no match).
Gates read mcp_tool_calls via _recent_call: the most recent row for the prerequisite with ok=1, blocked=0 and ts within _GATE_WINDOW_S (120s).

Arguments listed in _TRUNCATE_KEYS (mail compose body, imessage send message, vault write/append content) are logged to mcp_tool_calls.args_json as a _TRUNCATE_LEN (200) char prefix plus '... [N chars]' when longer than the cutoff; values at or under 200 chars are logged verbatim (task:593321f0).
mcp-tool-call-gates.description: Host-agnostic pre/post hook mechanism around every local-mac tool call, run by dispatcher.invoke (used by the MCP tools' _wrap and by the `mac` CLI) rather than relying on external settings.json hooks. Runs pre-check gates that can block a call outright, then logs every call's outcome to tool_hints.sqlite; the gates read that same log.
invariants: Gate state is the persisted mcp_tool_calls table, shared by every process that logs calls, so a prerequisite met in one process (MCP server or one `mac` invocation) satisfies a gate in another; it survives server restarts but only counts within 120s.
Gates fail closed: a failed log read, or a lost log write, counts as no prerequisite.
The 120s window is owned by this repo (_GATE_WINDOW_S); it does not mirror claude-hooks' gate_rules.yaml.
imessage__send requires a contacts__search within 120s whose found flag is True; mail__delete requires a mail__read within 120s (presence only).
Table schema (including the `found` column ALTER) is ensured once per process per DB path (_SCHEMA_READY).

Every _TRUNCATE_KEYS key must be a parameter of that (domain, action) handler, or redaction silently never matches; tests/test_tool_hooks_redact.py enforces this via dispatcher.resolve + inspect.signature.
mcp-tool-call-gates.name: mcp-tool-call-gates

contracts: handle_wait/handle_alarm return a message that includes the timer's pid; that pid is the handle handle_cancel takes.
handle_cancel(pid) sends SIGTERM to the whole process group of a live timer and returns 'Timer N cancelled'.
handle_cancel on a pid that no longer exists returns 'Timer N already finished' (success, so a cleanup that runs twice is harmless). A pid that never existed reads the same way.
handle_cancel raises ValueError ('Not a timer') for pid <= 1 or a live pid that is not a timer, and never signals it.
time-tools-timers.description: Clock, wait/alarm timers and sounds. wait and alarm schedule a notification by starting a detached `sh` polling loop that leads its own process group and report its pid. cancel stops that group by pid.
invariants: A timer is recognised by its shape: pgid == pid and `ps -o command=` starting with _TIMER_COMMAND. _TIMER_COMMAND must stay in step with the script _schedule builds, or cancel refuses every timer.
play_sound also uses _spawn_detached but reports no pid and is not cancellable.
time-tools-timers.name: time-tools-timers
